configs.description: The 7050SX3-48YC12 with two AC supplies and front-to-rear air: PWR-500AC-F supplies and FAN-7000H-F fan modules, all with red handles. Ordered as DCS-7050SX3-48YC12-F.
configs.name: f

gaps.note: Guide Table 1 gives a depth of 44.4 cm (17.5 in) and the data sheet 44.6 cm. The guide's is modelled; the difference is 2 mm.
gaps.wanted: the maker's statement of which is current.

gaps.note: Storage temperature -25 to 70 C (guide Table 2) against -40 to 70 C (data sheet). The guide's is in attrs.
gaps.wanted: the maker's statement of which is current.

gaps.note: The guide draws four generic rear panels (Figures D-1 to D-4) and does not say which model uses which. The 7050SX3-48YC12 is mapped to D-2 by its four fans (data sheet), its two supplies and its rear management ports. The data sheet's "Rear View" photograph (PDF page 3) shows the same shape but is a thumbnail.
gaps.wanted: the maker's statement of the rear panel of the 7050SX3-48YC12.

gaps.note: The guide's Figures 3-1 to 3-14 are isometric drawings with no measure and the kit guides for KIT-7001, KIT-7101 and the other spares are not held, so no ear position or rail kit is written.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned drawing of the mounting bracket position, and the kit guides.

gaps.note: Figure C-14 is too small to resolve any per-port lamp, so none is modelled and the port lamp states of guide Appendix A.1.2 are not attached to a port.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the lit face.

gaps.note: The speed bands' legends, the small print over the cages, the yellow port-speed group outlines, the lamp glyphs and the model line are unreadable or barely readable in the 576 px figure. The model text is set; the rest is not drawn.

Which side the latches of the stacked cages face, and whether the third row is upright, is not visible in the figure. The library's belly-to-belly convention is used for the first two rows and the third row is upright.
The management block's console symbol is drawn as the 7280SR3-48YC8 draws it; the figure resolves the block only as three stacked ports.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the rear management block.

gaps.note: The data sheet spares list PWR-500AC-R, PWR-500-DC-R and FAN-7000H-R; the data sheet's ordering information lists only a -F build of this model. The guide draws red handles only, so the blue reverse parts are not modelled.
gaps.wanted: a picture of the reverse-airflow supply and fan module.

gaps.note: The guide's Figure D-2 draws one generic supply (the AC one, an inlet and a fan guard with a red handle). The PWR-500-DC is the AC housing with a plain two-pole terminal block; the guide shows a DC supply only in isometric figures.
gaps.wanted: a flat drawing or photograph of the PWR-500AC and PWR-500-DC.

gaps.note: The guide's power tables and the data sheet give whole-switch figures only; the fan modules' missing power figure (lint L27) stands. The supplies state their output.

Guide Table 5 says "Attach ground directly to back" and Figures 4-1 and 4-2 show an earth grounding pad on the rear, and callout 9 of Figure D-2 names it; the pad is not drawn flat anywhere, so none is placed.
gaps.wanted: a flat drawing of the rear with the grounding pad.

chassis.note: Guide Table 1: 48.3 x 4.4 x 44.4 cm (19 x 1.75 x 17.5 inches), 9.2 kg (20.3 lbs). Data sheet: 44 x 4.4 x 44.6 cm, 20.3 lbs (9.22 kg). The width: 48.3 cm is over the mounting ears, so the body between them, which is what is modelled, is the data sheet's 44 cm (440.0 here). The height is 43.7, as the library's other 7050 devices. The depth is the guide's 44.4 cm (444.0), which agrees with the guide's 17.5 inches; the data sheet's 44.6 cm is 2 mm more: the gap `depth`. The weights agree (9.2 kg and 9.22 kg). 1RU.

colour.note: The front plate is the median of the grey pixels (neither black nor white, low saturation) of the guide's figure C-14, #737373. The figure is a raster and its lighting is not known, so the shade is estimated.

configurations.note: Data sheet ordering information: DCS-7050SX3-48YC12-F ("front-to-rear air, 2xAC") and the "#" SKU ("configurable fans and psu"); there is no -R SKU. The "#" SKU is an order of parts, not a part number a DCIM can hold. The data sheet lists no DC build of the switch: the PWR-500-DC-F supply is a spare, so the DC configuration is an example with no part number.

ears.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide's Chapter 3 mounts the switch with the accessory-kit brackets and shows them in isometric drawings that carry no measure, and the kit guides are not held. Recorded in the gap rack-ears.

environment.note: Guide Table 2: operating 0 to 40 C, storage -25 to 70 C, altitude 0 to 3,000 m, humidity 5 to 90 percent non-condensing. Data sheet: storage -40 to 70 C. The storage temperature differs: gap `environment`, the guide's used.

front-legend.note: The figure prints the maker's wordmark and the model line up the left plate. THE WORDMARK IS NOT DRAWN: a logo-zone region is reserved over it and the plain model text is set.

front-ports.note: Figure C-14 at 1.298 px/mm. Forty-eight SFP cages in three rows. Rows one and two (the odd number on top, ports 1 to 32) are four groups of two columns at each end of the face: the yellow group outlines start 6.9, 40.3, 73.7 and 107.1 mm across at the left and 291.8, 325.2, 358.6 and 392.0 mm at the right, a 33.4 mm step, and the first cage of each group is 9.0 mm inside the outline's edge, so the cages stand on the registry's 14.25 mm ganged-SFP pitch with a 4.9 mm gap between groups. The third row (ports 33 to 48) puts two cages under each group in the same columns. The rows read centred 11.8, 24.1 and 37.0 mm down, so the cages are 6.6, 18.9 and 31.8 mm from the top. Twelve QSFP100 cages in two stacked rows of six columns (49 to 60) in three groups of two, the first columns reading 156.4, 201.2 and 252.0 mm across (the groups are not evenly spaced in the figure: a grey vent column stands between the first and second), on the registry's 19.0 mm pitch inside a group; the rows read centred 12.4 and 25.5 mm down. The belly-to-belly orientation is the library's convention (upper cage upright, lower turned 180; the third row upright); the figure is too small to show the latch side.

fru-bays.note: Guide Appendix E (E.2 power supplies, E.3 fan modules) and the data sheet ("1+1 hot-swappable power supplies and four N+1 hot-swap fans"): THE TWO POWER SUPPLIES AND THE FOUR FAN MODULES ARE BAYS. Nothing on this chassis is a built-in unit. The management block, the USB port and the console port are part of the chassis and are placements.

gate-1-front.note: Figure C-14 passes. The raster is 576 x 141 pixels; the body between its plate edges measures 571 px wide and 55 px tall (aspect 10.4) against the data sheet's 440 / 43.7 = 10.07, so the figure is near-orthographic along its width and carries geometry at 1.298 px/mm (the 440 mm body is the scale anchor); it reads about 3 percent tall, so the rows are the less sure axis. One pixel is 0.77 mm, so every position is good to about 1 mm along the face and 1.5 mm down it, and every one is `estimated` because it is read off a picture and no dimension states it. The cages were read from the white port-number tabs in a three-times enlargement.

gate-1-rear.note: Figure D-2 is a 552 x 115 px raster whose chassis is 549 px between its edges (1.248 px/mm over the 440 mm body); positions are good to about 1 mm. The guide draws the rear generically (D-1 to D-4) and does not say which model uses which. The 7050SX3-48YC12 is mapped to D-2 by its four fan modules (data sheet: "Hot-swappable Fans 4 (N+1 redundant)"), its 1RU height, its two supplies and its management ports at the rear (Figure C-14 draws none at the front). The data sheet (PDF page 3) captions a rear photograph for the 7050SX3-48YC12, a supply, the management block, four fan modules and a supply, which agrees; the guide does not name the figure, so THE MAPPING IS ESTIMATED.

interface-names.note: Not printed and not modelled. EOS names ports Ethernet1 to Ethernet60 and Management1; this is the vendor's convention and no held document prints it.

lifecycle.note: Searched the held documents (the guide and the data sheet) for an end-of-sale or end-of-life notice for the 7050SX3-48YC12: none. No web search was made, so this is a statement about those documents only.

other-faces.note: No source draws the top, bottom or sides flat. The guide's installation figures are isometric. Each carries an `empty` sentence. The guide's Table 5 says "Attach ground directly to back" for this model (Figures 4-1 and 4-2, the earth grounding pad on the rear); no figure measures it.

port-lamps.note: Guide Appendix A.1.2 gives the port lamp states of the family. Figure C-14 draws small lamps at the corner of each cage that cannot be placed or counted at 1.3 px/mm. No port lamp is modelled (gap `port-lamps`).

port-numbering.note: Figure C-14 (callout 5, "Port numbers") prints 1 over 2, 3 over 4 across the first four groups and 17 over 18 across the last four, with 33 and 34 under the first group and so on to 40, and 41 to 48 under the last four; the QSFP cages are 49 over 50 to 59 over 60. The odd number is the upper cage. The figure prints each number on a white tab over its cage; a seated cage hides what is painted under it, so the numerals are set in the band between the rows (the odd number left of its column centre and the even one right of it; the third row's in the band above it). EOS interface names are not printed on the metal and are not modelled.

port-speed-groups.note: Guide section C.1 and Figure C-14 (callout 6, "Port-speed group"): the SFP cages are grouped, and the data sheet says "the high density SFP ports can be configured in groups of 4 to run either at 25G or a mix of 10G/1G speeds". The figure outlines each group of four (two columns of two rows) in yellow; the outlines are not drawn and the speed of each port is modelled at the highest native rate, 25G.

power.note: Guide Table 4: typical / maximum 170 W / 325 W with PWR-500AC or PWR-500-DC. The data sheet prints the same, 170W / 325W ("measured at 25C ambient with 50% load on all ports, excludes transceivers"): the documents agree and there is no conflict.

rear.note: Figure D-2 at 1.248 px/mm, the rear seen from behind with x = 0 at the left of the drawing. PS1 is the left and PS2 the right. Each supply reads about 88 mm wide in the figure (taken as arista/7050x3-pwr-500-ac's 86.5 mm) at 4.0 and 346.0 mm across and 1.85 mm down, an inlet at the left and a fan guard with a red diagonal handle at the right. The management block is a grey plate 94.5 to 116.0 mm across with the Ethernet management port, the USB port and the RJ-45 console port stacked in it. Four fan modules with the grilles starting 117.3, 175.3, 229.1 and 286.5 mm across, taken as a 56.4 mm pitch from 117.3 mm (each a grille, a red handle and a label tab), at 2.55 mm down.

rear-fan.note: Data sheet: "Hot-swappable Fans 4 (N+1 redundant)", "Fan Tray FAN-7000H-F" and the spare FAN-7000H-F (front-to-rear). The four fan modules are bays that accept FAN-7000H-F, the same component as arista/7050cx3-32s seats (one maker part number, one component).

sources.note: 7050 Series 1RU (Gen 3) Quick Start Guide, Arista Networks, document DOC-00141-08, 57 pages, copyright 2025, PDF created 2025-08-19 (https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/qsg/qsg-books/QS_7050_1RU_Gen3.pdf): Table 1 (dimensions and weights), Table 2 (operating and storage), Table 3 (power input), Table 4 (power draw and supported supplies), section 2.1 (airflow orientation, handle colour), section 4.1 and Table 5 (grounding), section C.1 (port-speed groups), Appendix C (Figure C-14, the front panel of the DCS-7050SX3-48YC12), Appendix D (Figure D-2, the rear panel with management ports in the rear), Appendix E (field replacement). 7050X3 Series 10/25/40/50/100G Data Center Switches Data Sheet, Arista Networks, 03-0040-46 (https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/Datasheets/7050X3-Datasheet.pdf): the model comparison, the power supply specifications and the ordering information. Held and checked first: intake COVERAGE.md and SOURCES.md, which list no photograph, 3D model or CAD file for this model (Arista publishes none; a `find` of the intake folder for 3D files found none) and a Visio stencil master that was not used. No drawing, photograph or logo is copied into the library, only transcribed facts and new drawings.

speed-strips.note: Figure C-14 draws a cyan band between the second and third rows under each end block and a lavender band under the QSFP block, with tiny legends. The bands are drawn in those colours at 29.5 and 31.0 mm down; the legends are unreadable and are not drawn.

status-lamps.note: Figure C-14 callouts 1 to 4: a system status lamp, a fan status lamp and a status lamp for each of the two power supplies, four lamps in a column at the far right, 427.5 mm across and 4.0, 7.2, 10.4 and 13.6 mm down; the order (system, fan, PS1, PS2) is the callout order of the figure.

vents.note: The figure shows a perforated grey field under and around the QSFP block (about 34 to 43 mm down, 142 to 295 mm across) and a perforated column on each side of it. Only the lower field is drawn, in its measured extent, not hole by hole.
